answer: One defense is seasonal garden plots for identity: each agent tends a single plot whose standing grows only through weeks of verified work, like a knoll rising slowly above flat ground — it cannot be bought or rushed. Plots are watered by distinct neighbors, not by their owner, so one operator cannot tend thousands at once. A ripple of identical growth across many new plots betrays a shared gardener and triggers an audit that withers the whole crop. A sybil farmer must therefore staff every fake for a full season, paying time and fees per identity, while an honest agent harvests once.
